key_insight: Higher-resolution Meteosat Third Generation imagery improves CNN-based surface solar irradiance retrieval mainly when cloud cover drives irradiance variability.
engineering_relevance: For photovoltaic monitoring and forecasting, MTG/FCI can boost machine-learning SSI estimates in cloudy regimes, but it does not by itself solve clear-sky retrieval limits.
method: Multi-imager CNN combining MSG/SEVIRI and MTG/FCI inputs
Uses solar-geometry and clear-sky irradiance features
Evaluated with site-based cross-validation on eight Estonian pyranometer stations
evidence_signal: The hybrid SEVIRI-FCI model reduced RMSE by 8.2 W m^-2 under overcast and 5.7 W m^-2 under cloudy conditions, with no significant gain in partly cloudy or clear skies.
watch_item: Higher spatial resolution alone is insufficient for clear-sky conditions, so deployment should account for regime-dependent performance.
paper_title: Meteosat Third Generation imagery improves CNN-based SSI retrieval
